title: Herbrand extraction for equality-free existential sequents

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)

summary: Extract finite term-tuples and actual propositional factor proofs from equality-free existential theorems, with exact reconstruction and parameter boundaries.
abstract: A classical proof that something exists need not identify one term whose defining assertion is always true. It can instead supply a finite list of possible terms whose instances form a proved disjunction. For formulas without equality, with all existential quantifiers before a quantifier-free matrix, we extract such a list directly from the finite proof and retain a propositional proof of its alternatives. The same data reconstruct the existential theorem. Leading universal variables become arbitrary parameters in the extracted terms, while a temporary parameter may still be needed when the original language has no ground term. An explicit two-instance proof shows why the finite list cannot always be reduced to one candidate.
